blacklistabilityReview.evidence: 2026-07-30 re-review. EVM: at BSC block 113074656 (2026-07-30T20:34:28Z) token 0xdd73ea766b80417c0607a3f08e34a0c415d89d56 has zero EIP-1967 implementation slot; Sourcify ABIs on BSC/Base/Arbitrum expose only ERC20 + ERC20Burnable + AccessControl + ERC20Permit + mint (MINTER_ROLE), no pause, freeze, blacklist, blocklist, or arbitrary-holder-burn; paused() eth_call reverts; burnFrom is allowance-gated. Controlling authority on EVM is DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE/MINTER_ROLE (prior review: EOA 0xc122…0bc + mint/redeem 0x5D54…F22C). Movement (material): DefiLlama 2026-07-30 chain balances show Movement ~465086.70 of ~501682.76 listed supply (~92.7%). Both current package 0xf39c…1ff6 and legacy package 0xed80…f83d (DefiLlama Movement supply module; weusd::total_supply 465086.702603 at ledger block_height 80220565) store ManagedFungibleAsset with transfer_ref and burn_ref; Aptos FA docs allow TransferRef to freeze accounts and BurnRef to burn. Current package weusd_mint_redeem and weusd_cross_chain_gas expose admin pause/unpause (is_paused=false at review). Legacy package upgrade_number=17 with compatible policy 1, publisher can replace modules without on-chain timelock. Failure domain: PicWe package publishers / admin EOAs on each deployment; no third-party freeze oracle. Upstream: if/when reserves were USDC/USDC.e, Circle freeze would impair redemption collateral, but that is inherited collateral risk, not a WEUSD token-level blacklist. Direct holder freeze is therefore possible via Movement FA TransferRef (and mint-path pause), not a confirmed live all-holder freeze, and not present on EVM bytecode, asset-wide false is unsupported.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: WEUSD's bridge overlay is PicWe's own issuer-native burn-on-source / mint-on-destination route, distinct from the five deployments' independent native issuance assessed under Mint Authority. PicWe's cross-chain-transfer docs state that the source chain burns and the target chain mints through a self-built route with PicWe-operated keepers; no Wormhole, LayerZero, CCIP, canonical-rollup, or external validator network was found. Structured controls now cover the four EVM Cross-Chain contracts, the common PicWe admin EOA, the reviewed Base role-hash holder, the Movement cross-chain relayer, and the Movement package publisher's bridge-module upgrade authority. Keeper quorum, role semantics, replay protection, and complete operator membership remain unverified; the route has no verified independent prudential limit or third-party attestation.
